title: Sonar
primeWhy: The phone plays a steady tone near the top of hearing and listens for it coming back. Anything that moves bends the returning tone, and that bend is the whole measurement.
primePrivacy: The sound never leaves the phone — nothing is recorded and nothing is uploaded
logEmptyHint: Leave the phone listening and come back — every burst of motion lands here.
logClearBody: {n} recorded events will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
sigHonestTitle: What this can and cannot tell you
sigHonestReal: Motion in the room, its intensity relative to a still room, and — when the reading is decisive — whether it moves toward the phone or away.
sigHonestNot: Not distance, not direction in space, not how many people, not speed in m/s. A continuous tone carries none of those, and one microphone has no sense of where.
sigAudible: Younger ears often hear 19 kHz as a thin whine. Dogs and cats hear it clearly — to them this is a loud, sustained tone, not ultrasound.
sigAutoStop: Listening stops on its own after 5 minutes.
profTagline: Sonar turns the phone into an ultrasonic motion sensor. It emits a steady tone near 19 kHz from the speaker and watches the microphone for the Doppler sidebands anything moving reflects back. It learns what a still room scores, then reports motion relative to that — with direction when the signal is decisive, and honestly nothing else: no distance, no bearing, no speed. Everything is computed on the device; no recording is kept and nothing is uploaded.
installDesc: Works offline, opens like an app
installIosHint: In Safari: tap Share, then Add to Home Screen.
installGenericHint: In the browser menu choose Install or Add to Home Screen.
